chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ash-Shah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abu Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimy narrated to us, on the authority of his father, saying: Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), that he said in his will to him:

O Ali! In adultery there are six characteristics: three of them are in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world, it removes beauty/happiness, hastens destruction, and cuts off sustenance. And as for those in the Hereafter, it is bad reckoning, the wrath of the Merciful, and eternity in the Fire.
ai.seo_question: What are the six consequences of adultery in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith traces its chain back to the Prophet through the Imams, emphasizing the cosmic and physical toll of adultery. It categorizes the consequences into three worldly afflictions—loss of beauty, hastened death, and cut off sustenance—and three hereafter penalties: bad reckoning, divine wrath, and eternal Hellfire. This dual framework underscores the holistic impact of the sin on both the believer’s temporal existence and spiritual destiny.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-3 Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ash-Shah narrated that Abu Hamid quoted Abu Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimy, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his grandfather (MGB) that in his will to Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB), the Prophet (MGB) stated, “O Ali!

There are six characteristics in adultery: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. Those in this world are: it would take away happiness; speed up destruction; and cut off one’s daily sustenance. And those in the Hereafter are: it would make the Reckoning hard; cause the Wrath of the Merciful Lord; and result in residing in the Fire.”
